hyps.why: If edge 0 is none, node 1 gets no input, so a conv on edge 4 is on a dead path and adds nothing.
If edge 1 is none, edge 5 can only carry signal via the 0->1->2 path, so a conv there helps far less.
Edge 2 needs node 1 to carry signal, which requires edge 0, so the conv is useless when edge 0 is none.
Replacing none with a conv adds a new path, which gains more than replacing an existing op.
Adding a direct skip path where there was none gives a big gain in trainability and accuracy.
Removing an edge that is already dead costs nothing, whereas removing a live edge usually hurts.
Edge 5 is mostly dead when edge 1 is none, so removing it costs less than usual.
With edge 4 none, node 1 only feeds node 2, so the conv on edge 0 contributes through a longer and weaker route.
With edge 5 none, node 2's output reaches node 3 nowhere, so a conv on edge 1 is wasted.
Diminishing returns: when another conv path to the output already exists, an extra conv on the direct edge adds less.
